text: Write the `factor` rule, including the case that makes parentheses work. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: case LPAREN -> { Expr e = ___;      // start over at the top level
___;               // and insist on the closing bracket
explanation: Verified: `(2 + 3) * 4` parses to `(* (+ 2 3) 4)`. The `LPAREN` case is the recursion — the bottom level calls the top level, which is exactly what parentheses mean: inside brackets, begin again with no precedence context. And `expect(RPAREN)` is the only thing in the parser that makes brackets balance, working because the recursive call returns precisely when the inner expression is finished.
